summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of liver transplant, alcoholic cirrhosis, and chronic malnutrition, was transferred from an outside hospital intubated due to hypoxic respiratory failure and healthcare-associated pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. He was treated with intravenous vancomycin, meropenem, and amikacin, which was later de-escalated based on culture results. After successful extubation, a video swallow study revealed aspiration, leading to dietary modifications with soft solids and thin liquids using specific techniques to reduce aspiration risk. His chronic pain regimen was adjusted with oxycodone discontinued and oxycontin initiated. Sirolimus was reduced to 2 mg daily due to elevated levels, and iron supplementation was stopped due to iron overload on liver biopsy. He was discharged home with services on room air, with prescriptions for albuterol nebulizer, supplemental oxygen as needed, and follow-up with speech therapy and transplant clinic.
